# `opening-draft` commands

## `opening-draft apply`

Post a planned opening through the cutover engine, as one batch: the accounts' balances in one opening journal against a clearing account, each open invoice and bill for its open amount, each item's stock. All or nothing: a command refused part way undoes what the opening had posted (rolled_back). A run stopped any other way stays applying and the same call continues it. Refused while the plan has a blocking exception; `accept_differences` (a person's act; an agent needs the capability opening.accept-differences) posts one whose given totals do not tie, the difference left in the clearing account. Before `apply`, show your principal the plan's exact details once (the as-of date, the counts and totals, and which checks are given and which derived) and apply on their yes: an opening sets how the books start.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | import |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.apply` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow opening-draft apply 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Owner confirmed the plan's totals" --json`

{"command": "opening-draft apply", "input": {"draft": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK"}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

| `draft` | `DRAFT` | string | yes | no | — | The draft.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |
| `accept_differences` | `--accept-differences` | boolean | no | no | false | Post the opening although a total you gave does not tie to its rows (receivables, payables or stock), or the equity you typed does not balance: the difference stays in the clearing account in plain sight and tie-out says not tied until it is cleared. A person's act: an agent needs the capability opening.accept-differences granted by its principal. |

## `opening-draft create`

Start guided opening balances for a business with no old books: keep what the owner knows as of the cutover date, each step as rows with a header row, pasted or typed: `balances` (Account, Balance: every bank, card, loan and other account balance you know, on the account's own side unless a Side column says debit or credit; type equity accounts only if you know them, else equity is worked out), `open_invoices` (Customer, Number, Date, Due date or Terms, Open amount, PO number, Memo), `unpaid_bills` (Vendor, Reference, Date, Due date or Terms, Open amount, Memo), `stock` (Item, Quantity, Total value or Unit cost). Give `given` totals (receivables, payables, stock) to check the rows against; a total left out is taken from the rows and labelled derived. Nothing posts: then `opening-draft plan`. Example: {"as_of": "2026-09-30", "balances": {"content": "Account\tBalance\nChecking\t12430.55\n"}, "given": {"payables": "3100.00"}}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | import |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.create` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow opening-draft create 2026-09-30 --balances '{"content": "Account,Balance\nChecking,12430.55\n"}' --given '{"payables": "3100.00"}' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Owner's opening figures" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```

## `opening-draft discard`

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

## `opening-draft plan`

Plan a draft through the cutover engine, writing nothing to the books: every record it would make, the opening journal, the clearing account's parts and the checks, each `given` (a figure the owner gave, checked against the rows) or `derived` (taken from the rows; nothing independent checks it), and every exception, blocking first. `ready` is true when nothing blocks. Before `apply`, show your principal the plan's exact details once (the as-of date, the counts and totals, and which checks are given and which derived) and apply on their yes: an opening sets how the books start.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | import |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.plan` |
| External binary body | none |

`bookflow opening-draft plan 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Plan the opening" --json`

```

### Input

## `opening-draft reverse`

Undo an applied opening as one unit through its batch, for as long as nothing later depends on it: each invoice, credit memo, bill, journal and sales receipt deleted with its history kept, each vendor credit and stock adjustment voided, each customer, vendor, item and term it made renamed and deactivated. Accounts are not retired (an account keeps its history): the clearing account stays at 0.00 for the next opening; `stays` lists that and anything else the opening set outside its batch. Refused (E_BATCH_BLOCKED), naming each record and what clears it, while one is in use (a payment applied to an opening invoice, stock it brought in sold since) or was changed since; then nothing changes. Needs your own delete grants for those families. --dry-run shows the plan and a fingerprint. Confirm with your principal first.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | import |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.reverse` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow opening-draft reverse 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Wrong opening date" --dry-run --json`

### MCP

```

## `opening-draft tie-out`

Prove an applied opening: the books as of the cutover date against every figure, each check `given` ("tied to the 12,430.55 you gave") or `derived` ("taken from your invoice list; not independently checked"), receivables and payables by customer and vendor, stock by item, and the clearing account at 0.00. `tied` needs every check tied and the clearing account at 0.00. Writes nothing.

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_QUERY_STALE` | The company changed since this query began; restart without a cursor. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |

## `opening-draft update`

Change a draft not yet applied: a step's rows (an empty `content` clears the step), the cutover date, the totals given, the stock items confirmed to make, the clearing account. Carries the version read. The draft returns to `draft` and needs a new plan. Example: {"draft": "01J...", "expected_version": 2, "open_invoices": {"content": "Customer,Number,Date,Terms,Open amount\nAcme,1001,09/02/2026,Net 30,412.50\n"}}.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | import |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.update` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow opening-draft update 01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK --expected-version 1 --unpaid-bills '{"content": "Vendor,Reference,Date,Terms,Open amount\nFerguson Supply,INV-1,09/10/2026,Net 30,3100.00\n"}' --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Owner's opening figures" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "opening-draft update", "input": {"draft": "01J9ZK4QF8T7E2V5N3B6C1D0BK", "expected_version": 1, "unpaid_bills": {"content": "Vendor,Reference,Date,Terms,Open amount\nFerguson Supply,INV-1,09/10/2026,Net 30,3100.00\n"}}, "company": "Company ID or name", "dry_run": true, "reason": "Preview the requested change"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `draft` | `DRAFT` | string | yes | no | — | The draft.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | The version you read; a draft changed meanwhile is refused.; minimum 1 |
| `as_of` | `--as-of` | string \| null | no | yes | null | A new cutover date. |
| `label` | `--label` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |
| `balances.content` | `--balances-content` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The rows as pasted or typed, with a header row: tab text from a spreadsheet, or comma or semicolon separated. Give this or `attachment`; an empty string clears the step. |
| `balances.attachment` | `--balances-attachment` | string \| null | no | yes | null | An attachment of this company holding the rows as a CSV file. |
| `balances.date_order` | `--balances-date-order` | literal["MDY", "DMY", "YMD"] \| null | no | yes | null | The order of day and month in the dates when no date tells (03/04/2026): MDY month first, DMY day first. |
| `open_invoices.content` | `--open-invoices-content` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The rows as pasted or typed, with a header row: tab text from a spreadsheet, or comma or semicolon separated. Give this or `attachment`; an empty string clears the step. |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/opening-draft.update`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `label` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `as_of` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `state` | literal["draft", "planned", "applying", "applied", "rolled_back", "failed", "reversed", "discarded"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `version` | integer | yes | no | — | — |
| `steps` | array[object] | yes | no | — | Each step given, in the order of the guided page |
| `steps[].step` | literal["balances", "open_invoices", "unpaid_bills", "stock"] | yes | no | — | — |
| `steps[].kind` | string | yes | no | — | The cutover file kind the rows are read as |
| `steps[].source` | literal["content", "attachment"] | yes | no | — | Pasted text, or an attachment |
| `steps[].attachment` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `steps[].date_order` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `steps[].rows` | integer | yes | no | — | Rows read |
| `steps[].content` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The pasted text, as kept; null for an attachment |
| `steps[].problems` | array[object[string, any]] | yes | no | — | What the rows alone show to be wrong, each with its line, code and problem; the plan checks them against the books |
| `given` | object[string, object \| null] | yes | no | — | Totals given to check against; null where left to the rows |
| `make_items` | array[string] | yes | no | — | — |
| `clearing_account` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `batch` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | The batch the opening posted in; reverse it as one unit |
| `summary` | object[string, any] \| null | yes | yes | — | The last plan or apply: ready, counts, checks, blocking lines |
| `created_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `updated_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `applied_at` | string \| null | yes | yes | — | — |
| `next` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The command to run next, or null |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "applied_at": null,
  "as_of": "value",
  "batch": null,
  "clearing_account": null,
  "created_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "given": {},
  "id": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "label": "value",
  "make_items": [],
  "next": null,
  "state": "draft",
  "steps": [],
  "summary": null,
  "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "version": 1
}
```

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_COMPANY_AMBIGUOUS` | More than one company matches; use the id or Organization/Company. |
| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |
| `E_CONFIG_INVALID` | The configuration file could not be read. |
| `E_CONTEXT_IN_INPUT` | Input contains a context field. |
| `E_DB_BUSY` | Another Bookflow command is running on this data root. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_INACTIVE` | That directive has been deactivated. |
| `E_DIRECTIVE_NOT_FOUND` | No such directive. |
| `E_FEATURE_DISABLED` | This feature is not enabled for the company. |
| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_SHARE` | The path is on a network filesystem, which Bookflow refuses to use. |
| `E_NOT_INITIALIZED` | The data root is not initialized; run `bookflow init`. |
| `E_NO_ACTOR` | This login is not mapped to a Bookflow user. |
| `E_ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND` | No such organization. |
| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |
| `E_REASON_REQUIRED` | This write needs a reason: a short phrase naming what triggered it (--reason on the CLI, a top-level reason on MCP, the X-Bookflow-Reason header on HTTP). |
| `E_RECORD_NOT_FOUND` | No such record. |
| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
| `E_UNAUTHENTICATED` | No valid credential: log in, or send a bearer token. |
| `E_USAGE` | Invalid command syntax. |
| `E_VALIDATION` | Invalid input. |
| `E_VERSION_CONFLICT` | The record changed since the version you read. |
